title: Vickers Wellington X HF465
memorial_details:
Black tablet on a small grey brick plinth in semicircular, kerbed flower bed.

IBCC gives the date as 28 October 1944; the memorial inscription, as transcribed by IWM, reads 20 October 1944.

The black tablet in a lay-by on the A51 was built by volunteers from donated materials and dedicated in October 2003.
inscription: R.A.F. / WELLINGTON X, HF 465 OF 12 O.T.U. / DISINTEGRATED OVER BRIDGEMERE 20. 10. 1944 / IN MEMORY OF THE R.A.F.V.R. CREW
narrative: Wellington X HF465 of 12 Operational Training Unit, based at Chipping Warden, was on a daytime training flight when it broke up over Bridgemere, Cheshire. IBCC records the cause as loss of control while descending through cloud. Seven men were aboard and six died. The six who died were Flight Sergeant Leonard Joseph Timperley (pilot, 20), Pilot Officer Cecil Frank Holmes (29), and Sergeants Laurence Edwin Harrison (24), James David Milne (32), Arthur Fred Baker (35) and Ronald Whiteley (23). Timperley is buried at Chester (Blacon) Cemetery. IWM spells the third sergeant's surname Milnes; IBCC and the local history page give Milne. The navigator, Sergeant Douglas Hollis Wilson, survived; IBCC says the aircraft threw him clear, while a local news item says he baled out before it broke up.

external_narratives.summary: IWM record and our capture. Gives the inscription and seven names on the stone, six crew and a survivor heading.
Loss record for the pilot. Gives date, unit, take-off station, cause and the five other dead by surname. The other IBCC records were rate-limited and not read in full.
Local history page naming the crew with roles and ages, the survivor, the cause as judged by the writer, and how the memorial came about.

community_connection: The inscription names the crew as RAFVR and lists the survivor separately. A local history page says it came about after Marjorie Harrison, widow of Sergeant Harrison, visited the site in 2000.
